definitions.explanation: A tub filled with hot water for bathing. In Japan, the bath is for soaking after washing outside the tub.
The act of taking a bath, an important daily ritual in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: お{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}りましたか。
お{風呂|ふろ}を{沸|わ}かしてください。
{毎日|まいにち}お{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}ります。
examples.english: I take a bath every day.

examples.japanese: お{風呂|ふろ}は{熱|あつ}いですか。
お{風呂|ふろ}から{出|で}たら、{電話|でんわ}してください。
examples.english: Please call me when you get out of the bath.

examples.japanese: お{風呂|ふろ}が{沸|わ}きました。
お{風呂|ふろ}を{洗|あら}う。
{寝|ね}る{前|まえ}にお{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: I take a bath before going to bed.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}ではお{風呂|ふろ}が{長|なが}い。
examples.english: In Japan, people take long baths.

examples.japanese: お{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}ってさっぱりした。
examples.english: I felt refreshed after taking a bath.

examples.japanese: お{風呂|ふろ}の{水|みず}を{入|い}れてください。
examples.english: Please fill the bathtub with water.

notes:
お{風呂|ふろ} refers to both the bathtub and the act of bathing. The お is an honorific prefix commonly used with this word.

JAPANESE BATHING CULTURE:
Wash and rinse your body outside the tub before soaking. The bath water is often shared by family members.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- お{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}る: to take a bath
- お{風呂|ふろ}を{沸|わ}かす: to heat the bath
- お{風呂|ふろ}から{上|あ}がる: to get out of the bath

RELATED TERMS:
- {銭湯|せんとう}: public bathhouse
- {温泉|おんせん}: hot spring
- {露天風呂|ろてんぶろ}: outdoor bath
- シャワー: shower
